headline: Xi ends three days in DC with a look at the Constitution
summary: Xi Jinping's state visit ended Friday with a tour of the National Archives alongside Trump, where the Declaration, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights are kept. It was his first state visit to the US in more than a decade. PBS NewsHour called the three days heavy on pageantry and light on policy. Xi said he'll see Trump again soon.

cover_question.q: What did they actually agree on?

cover_answer: Little that was announced. Xi says they'll meet again soon.
table_question: Is a party where nobody agrees on anything still worth throwing?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The leader of China, Xi Jinping, visited America for three days and went home today. On his last stop he and the president looked at the Constitution, the old paper that says how our country works. It's like showing a visitor the family photo album before they go. The two of them say they'll meet again soon.
5-7.why: A visit, a last stop, a goodbye. The old paper is the thing they can picture.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid thing for the whole event, so the script hands them the old paper and the photo album at the door, a goodbye they have watched at home. Three days of ceremony collapse into one last stop. Expect "is he coming back?" He says he'll see the president again soon, and that is all anyone has promised.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A state visit runs like a wedding: arrival, dinner, meetings, a last stop, a goodbye. Xi's ended Friday at the National Archives. PBS NewsHour counted three days of pageantry and few announcements. Some Republicans grumbled at the welcome.
8-12.why: The wedding gives them the steps. Then ask what the steps were for.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out how events run and whether the rules hold, so the script gives them the wedding, a ceremony with a set order, and lets them notice the order ran without a result. Expect "so what was the point?" The show may be the point, and PBS NewsHour's count, three days and few announcements, is the fact to sit with.

13-17.script: When is a lot of ceremony and few deals a success? Xi's first state visit in over a decade ended Friday with a promise to meet again. Second: some Republicans say the welcome jarred while Americans feel squeezed. Fair, or is the welcome the work?
13-17.why: Two arguable questions, and a Republican is asking the second.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: a visit that announced almost nothing can still matter, and the welcome can still look wrong at home. The script gives them the decade-long gap and the promise to meet again as the case for, and the grumbling as the case against. Expect "did Trump get anything?" Nothing announced, per PBS. Say so.

5-7.a: The biggest kind of visit one country's leader can pay another, with a fancy dinner and a lot of ceremony. Xi's lasted three days.

8-12.q: What did they actually agree on?
8-12.a: Little that was announced. PBS NewsHour called it heavy on pageantry, light on policy. Xi says they'll meet again.
It keeps the Declaration, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights. It was the visit's last stop.

13-17.a: The Hill reports some GOP lawmakers bristled at the lavish treatment while the country feels economic pressure.
Depends what you count. Few announcements, but a first state visit in over a decade and a promise to meet again.
